Alex —

Thanks — attaching the subprocessor inventory you asked for (CSV) and our SOC 2 Type II summary. High-level notes on subprocessors and data boundaries below to help Legal/Security triage quickly: 

Redwood subprocessor highlights (abridged):
- AWS (us-west-2): compute + object storage (customer data encrypted at rest with customer keys where requested).
- Google Cloud (us-central1): optional training/ML infra for internal evaluation (only used with explicit customer opt-in).
- Datadog: monitoring (aggregated metrics, application traces; no customer PII retained).
- Sentry: error reporting (scrubbed errors; ability to opt-out per customer).
- Postgres managed (RDS): metadata and index stores (encrypted).

Data sharing boundaries: customer content is segregated per-tenant; we use prefix/namespace isolation for KV caches and disk. Logs and telemetry are aggregated and retained for 90 days by default; longer retention available on request. Keys: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption-at-rest in Dedicated/Private deployments.

I’ve started filling your vendor questionnaire (link below) and uploaded the draft to the HubSpot deal record. Here’s the direct link to our public vendor questionnaire if you want to pre-review: https://redwood.com/security/vendor-questionnaire?prefill=acme.

Next steps:
- We’ll complete the attached questionnaire and return within 2 business days.
- Marcus/Rishi will prepare a short technical addendum on key management and residency for Legal.
- Let us know preferred time for the 30-min follow-up (we proposed Thursday morning).

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_2027-02-11.csv, SOC2-typeII-2026-redwood-summary.pdf
